newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to halt trade in mystery surging stocks.
newsitem.headline: Manila to halt trade in mystery surging stocks.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Friday it will stop trading in shares surging to the ceiling or floor price limits unless the movements are explained by the company.

"Whenever an issue reaches its ceiling or floor price limits during a particular trading day, a trading halt shall be imposed by the exchange on the following day unless the issuer discloses the reasons why its prices moved towards the limits," PSE chief operating officer Rafael Llave said in a circular.
The Manila bourse automatically freezes the share price of an issue when it shoots up by about 50 percent or falls by about 40 percent within a single trading day.
Llave said the bourse will ask companies to explain any unusual movements and only when responses are disseminated to member-brokers will trading on the counter be allowed to resume.
Although the PSE official did not say why the bourse issued the circular, the development comes on the heels of several unexplained surges in thirdliner issues.
Letters from the bourse seeking an explanation from the firms have mostly yielded a standard response saying company officials had no idea why it was happening.
